title: I Heard it on TikTok: Cross-Sectional Analysis of Quality of Social Media Content on Gender-Affirming Medical Treatment
screen_reason: Abstract-only text. Cross-sectional analysis of the top 100 most popular TikTok videos for each of three hashtags (#genderaffirmingcare, #hrt, #pubertyblockers): 300 pulled, 251 met inclusion criteria, and each video was classified Personal (personal experience), Useful (accurate information) or Misleading (inaccurate information), with inter-rater kappa 0.807. The abstract reports a verbatim share of items classified as carrying inaccurate information (50/251 = 20 %, headlined as 'One in five'), which is a share of items judged for accuracy with a stated denominator, so CONTENT. Only the abstract was available, so the ground-truth benchmark (which clinical guidance the accuracy judgement rested on) could not be verified.

estimates.date: Not stated in the abstract (article published 2025)
estimates.measure_type: % of popular TikTok videos on gender-affirming medical treatment classified as Misleading (containing inaccurate information)
estimates.value_raw: 50 (20%) classified as Misleading, of 251 videos meeting inclusion criteria (Personal 52 %, n = 130; Useful 71, 28 %)
estimates.denominator: 251 TikTok videos meeting inclusion criteria, out of the 300 pulled as the top 100 most popular videos for each of #genderaffirmingcare, #hrt and #pubertyblockers
estimates.definition: video classified as 'Misleading', i.e. containing inaccurate information about gender-affirming medical treatment (as opposed to 'Useful' = accurate information, or 'Personal' = primarily personal experience)
estimates.misinfo_def: Videos primarily describing personal experience were classified as Personal, those with accurate information were classified as Useful, and those with inaccurate information were classified as Misleading.
estimates.source_quote: Of 300 videos pulled, 251 met inclusion criteria. Most were classified as Personal (52%, n = 130), with 71 (28%) classified as Useful, and 50 (20%) as Misleading. Classification agreement between raters was good (kappa statistic of 0.807).
estimates.page_loc: Abstract, Results and Conclusions (full text not available)
estimates.ground_truth_detail: Rater classification into Personal / Useful / Misleading with reported inter-rater agreement kappa = 0.807 ('good'). The abstract does not say how many raters coded, what their expertise was, or which clinical guidance the accuracy judgement was benchmarked against - the full text was not available to check.
estimates.moderator_quote: Methods The top 100 most popular videos from three hashtags (#genderaffirmingcare, #hrt, and #pubertyblockers) were reviewed.
estimates.notes: ABSTRACT-ONLY extraction; the value itself is verbatim, but no methods detail beyond the abstract could be checked, hence confidence medium. IMPORTANT DENOMINATOR POINT for an adjudicator: the 251-video denominator includes 130 videos (52 %) classified as Personal, i.e. personal-experience narratives that make no informational claim. The 20 % is therefore a share of ALL popular videos on these hashtags, not a share of the informational videos; among videos coded for information content (71 Useful + 50 Misleading = 121) the misleading share would be far higher, but that denominator is not stated in the abstract and computing it would breach R8, so it is not extracted. Rank-truncated sample (top 100 per hashtag) => denom_selection=curated. Data-collection date is not reported; year set to the 2025 publication year as instructed.

missed_or_uncertain: (1) The abstract states that non-healthcare professionals created most of the misleading videos, 'although not significantly more than healthcare professionals', and that of the misleading videos 'about half were created by supporters - and about half by opposers - of gender-affirming care'. These are compositions within the misleading set (no full denominator, and 'about half' is not a stated value), so no rows were created. (2) No shares are reported for the Personal category as a misinformation measure, and no engagement/view-weighted share is given, so there is no EXPOSURE row. (3) Data-collection dates, country, and the ground-truth standard are all absent from the abstract; if the full text becomes available, ground_truth_detail, date/year and possibly a within-informational-videos denominator should be revisited. (4) The 'Useful' 28 % share is the accuracy complement and is not a misinformation numerator, so it is not rowed.

rob.design: Cross-sectional TikTok content analysis (abstract only). Frame: the top 100 most popular videos for each of three hashtags (#genderaffirmingcare, #hrt, #pubertyblockers), 300 pulled, 251 meeting inclusion criteria (inclusion criteria not stated in the abstract). Coding: videos classified Personal / Useful / Misleading; inter-rater agreement reported as kappa 0.807; number of raters, rater expertise, blinding, and the external accuracy benchmark are not reported in the abstract. No data-collection date, no country, no engagement-weighted analysis. Rank-truncated (most-popular) sample, so not representative of all platform content on the topic.
